query: How do I label water shutoff valves?

goal.title: Write and attach identification labels to basement water shutoff valves
goal.description: Inspect the exposed water lines and valve handles above a basement work area. Write identifying text on small adhesive labels using a black marker, then peel and attach the labels near overhead valves. Carry a remaining label to the plumbing behind the laundry shelf and attach it there before returning to the worktable.
goal.final_state: Written labels are visible by the overhead valve handles and a label has been pressed onto the plumbing behind the laundry shelf. The marker lies on the table when the person returns; no water-flow test or valve repair is shown.
procedure: Look along the exposed basement pipes and point to the valve locations.
Write identifying text on several adhesive labels at the table.
Cap the marker and peel the first label.
Press labels onto successive overhead valve/pipe locations.
Carry a remaining label to the valves behind the laundry shelf and attach it.
Return to the table after checking the labeled plumbing.

phases.description: Look along the overhead pipes and point at the valve handles above the work area. Return attention to the labels on the table.
Use a black marker to write text on the small white labels, moving each completed label aside. Cap and put down the marker when writing is finished.
Peel labels at the table and press them near successive overhead valves. Carry another label across the laundry area to the plumbing behind the shelf, press it in place and return to the table.
